correctness.rationale: In invariant affine-hyperplane measure d sigma(u)dt, conditioning on meeting Delta_(n-1) biases u by its full vertex-height width, not by Haar normals. For any generic section each j-face corresponds to an (j+1)-simplex-face indexed by j+2 vertices meeting both sides; integrate its crossing offset length to obtain numerator sum_S int w_S(u)d sigma over common denominator int w_[n](u). Project a standard Gaussian vector to the sum-zero subspace; normalized radius is independent of Haar direction and subtracting the sample mean preserves ranges, yielding E f_j=binom(n,j+2) R_(j+2)/R_n and rank gap law P(K=k)=E(G_(k+1)-G_(k))/R_n. The face formula binom(n,j+2)-binom(K,j+2)-binom(n-K,j+2) is exact. For m=n^gamma, endpoint telescoping of Gaussian gaps plus quantile concentration G_(m+1)/sqrt(2logn)->-sqrt(1-gamma) with uniform L2 control yields P(log M/log n<=gamma)->1-sqrt(1-gamma), law 1-U^2. For fixed j the face formula gives f_j asymptotic to M n^(j+1)/(j+1)! in probability, hence joint log exponent j+2-U^2. Endpoint gamma=0,1 handled. Exact small-n binomial face identities checked independently, source verify.py inspected. R_2=2/sqrt(pi), R_n~2sqrt(2logn) gives mean n^2/(2sqrt(2pi log n)). No assertion for j growing with n or nonregular simplexes.
